findings.finding: Key: From sums: A+a=2(B+b) and after transfer A+a= B+b+10 ⇒ B+b=10, A+a=20. So a=20−A, b=10−B. Use product eqns: A·a=4B·b and A·(a−5)=B·(b+5). Substitute → A(20−A)=4B(10−B) and A(15−A)=B(15−B). Brute‑force A∈[1,15], B∈[1,10] gives only (A,B)=(10,5). Product of ages =10·5=50.

Key: From “give 5 sweets” condition, sums equal ⇒ (a+As)−(b+Bs)=10. Using Alice’s “double” sum: a+As=2(b+Bs) ⇒ b+Bs=10, a+As=20. Then solve integers with As≥5, Bs≥0: a·As=4b·Bs and a·(As−5)=b·(Bs+5). Unique solution: a=10, b=5, As=10, Bs=5. Product ages=10·5=50.
